q: Under no circumstances ___ the dragon's hoard.
explain: Under no circumstances → inversion: should you + verb. Example: Under no circumstances should you open it.

q: So fierce ___ that even the bravest knights fled.
explain: So + adjective fronted → inversion with be. Example: So bright was the light that we shut our eyes.

notes.did the dragon roar: Did roar doesn't follow an adjective.

q: ___ it not for your warning, I would be lost in these stacks forever.
explain: Were it not for = if it were not for (present). Example: Were it not for you, I'd be lost.

notes.Had: Had it not been for is the past version.
notes.Was: Was isn't used in this inversion.
notes.If: If needs 'were': If it were not for.

q: Much ___ I admire her work, I cannot endorse this book.
explain: Much as = although (very much). Example: Much as I'd love to, I can't.

q: Try ___ he might, he could not decipher the runes.
explain: Try as he might = however hard he tried. Example: Try as I might, I couldn't sleep.

q: The riddle, ___ answer had eluded scholars for centuries, was finally solved.
explain: Whose for possession. Example: a riddle whose answer is simple.

notes.of which: Of which needs 'the answer of which'.

q: Little did she suspect that the librarian ___ her all along.
explain: Past perfect continuous for a long action before a past moment. Example: He had been waiting all day.

q: It is imperative that the scroll ___ returned before dawn.
explain: Imperative that + subjunctive be. Example: It is imperative that she be told.

q: Not a single word ___ during the entire ceremony.
explain: Passive: was spoken (nobody spoke it). Example: Not a word was said.

notes.spoke: Spoke is active: a word can't speak.

q: The more obscure the text, ___ the scholars become.
explain: The + comparative, the + comparative. Example: The harder the puzzle, the happier I am.

q: No sooner had the clock struck midnight ___ the books began to whisper.
explain: No sooner had... than. Example: No sooner had I left than it rained.

q: Should the dragon ___, offer it a riddle.
explain: Should + subject + plain verb = if. Example: Should you see her, say hi.

q: She talks as though she ___ the library herself.
explain: As though + past simple for something unreal now. Example: He acts as though he were king.

q: Be that as it ___, the prophecy must be fulfilled.
explain: Be that as it may = even so (fixed phrase).

q: Only by reading between the lines ___ the poem's true meaning.
explain: Only by... → inversion: can one grasp. Example: Only by practising can you improve.

q: Scarcely ___ the final page when the candles went out.
explain: Scarcely had + subject + past participle ... when. Example: Scarcely had we begun when it rained.

notes.did he turn: Did turn isn't used with 'when' here.

q: Never before ___ such a breathtaking manuscript.
explain: Never before → inversion; past perfect for before then. Example: Never before had I seen snow.

q: Come what ___, the library will stay open.
explain: Come what may = whatever happens (fixed phrase).

q: It's not as though he ___ warned.
explain: It's not as though + past perfect = he WAS warned (so no excuse). Example: It's not as though I hadn't told you.

notes.wasn't being: Wasn't being is continuous and odd.

q: ___ though it was, the riddle had a simple answer.
explain: Adjective + though + it was = although it was... Example: Tired though she was, she kept going.

notes.Bafflingly: An adverb can't start this pattern.
notes.However baffling: However baffling needs 'it was' without though.

q: She would sooner ___ the post than compromise her principles.
explain: Would sooner + plain verb. Example: I'd sooner walk.

q: Were it ___ to emerge that the scroll was forged, the scandal would be immense.
explain: Were it ever to... = if it ever... (formal). Example: Were it ever to happen, we'd be ready.

q: So engrossed ___ in the book that she missed the last bell.
explain: So + adjective fronted → inversion: was she. Example: So tired was he that he slept at once.

notes.she had: Had doesn't go with engrossed here.
notes.did she: Did doesn't go with an adjective.

q: It is vital that no one ___ informed until the birthday surprise.
explain: Vital that + subjunctive be. Example: It's vital that he be ready.

q: Not that I ___, but wasn't the deadline yesterday?
explain: Not that I mind = I don't mind, but... (fixed). Example: Not that I mind, but you're late.

q: ___ the archivist not intervened, the letters would have been burnt.
explain: Had + subject + not + past participle = if... hadn't. Example: Had she not called, I'd have left.

notes.If: If needs 'had': If the archivist had not.

q: The dragon, far ___ being hostile, offered us tea.
explain: Far from + -ing = not at all. Example: Far from being angry, she laughed.

q: Little ___ the apprentice know that the book was enchanted.
explain: Little did + subject + plain verb. Example: Little did we know.

q: Only in the final chapter ___ the narrator's true identity revealed.
explain: Only in... → inversion; passive is revealed. Example: Only then is the secret told.

q: Such ___ the force of her argument that the whole class fell silent.
explain: Such + be + noun (inverted) + that. Example: Such was the noise that we left.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: Under no circumstances should the dragon be woken.
explain: Under no circumstances + should + subject.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: Try as he might, he could not open the door.
explain: Try as he might = however hard he tried.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: So vast was the library that we got lost.
explain: So + adjective + was + subject + that.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: Be that as it may, the quest must go on.
explain: Be that as it may = even so.

q: Build the sentence.
answer: Not a single page had the apprentice skipped.
explain: Negative object + inversion.

explain: Scarcely had… when (No sooner had… than).

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: No double negatives: couldn't hear anything.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: The + comparative…, the + comparative: the more…, the more…

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: Far from + -ing = not at all.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: imperative that + subjunctive be.

q: Tap the word that is wrong.
explain: Fixed phrase: come what may.

text: ___ though it was, the riddle had a ___ simple answer.
explain: Adjective + though + it was; adverb before an adjective.

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
text: Only by reading ___ the lines ___ one grasp the poem.
explain: read between the lines; Only by… can one…

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
text: Not that I ___, but the ___ was yesterday.
explain: Not that I mind (fixed); deadline = last day.

q: Fill the gaps with the words.
text: The dragon, far ___ hostile, served tea ___ any sign of anger.
explain: far from (not at all); without any sign.
